exposure: Robson classification system (based on parity, previous CS history, fetal presentation, gestational age, and onset of labor)
cohort: The study included 740 pregnant women who delivered at a tertiary care centre over a 6-month period, encompassing both vaginal and Caesarean deliveries.
finding: The overall Caesarean section rate was 74.56%, and Robson groups 5, 2, and 4 were identified as the highest contributors to CS rates.
mod_finding: Repeat Caesarean section was found to contribute most to the overall CS rate, prompting recommendations to avoid medically unnecessary primary CS and promote vaginal births after prior CS.
